preconditions.expression: isinstance(starting_string, str) and isinstance(n, int) and n >= 1
preconditions.description: The `starting_string` must be a non-empty string, and `n` must be a positive integer.

postconditions.expression: all(len(look_and_say_sequence(starting_string, k)) > 0 for k in range(1, n))
postconditions.description: For every integer `k` from 1 to `n-1`, the intermediate sequence elements are non-empty strings.

postconditions.expression: return_value == starting_string if n == 1 else return_value == look_and_say_sequence(look_and_say_sequence(starting_string, n - 1), 1)
postconditions.description: The result is the `n`-th element of the look-and-say sequence starting from `starting_string`, where each element is generated by reading the previous element and describing consecutive digits (e.g., '11' becomes '21', '22' remains '22').

postconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789' for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: The result string consists only of digits (0-9).
